title: Burst policy & forecast 1:1 - scratch
content:
Purpose:
- Quick prep notes for 1:1 with Marcus (capacity owner) / Sofia (billing ops). Iterate on burst policy and reservation sizing for Q2 sprint.
- Capture hypotheses to test in sim job before committing to any reserved capacity changes.

Meeting goals (30m):
1) Align on a conservative burst policy that limits cost while preserving 99th percentile latency SLO.
2) Pick a forecast scenario (A/B/C) to use for next-week dedicated reservation proposal.
3) Identify 3 immediate experiments to validate assumptions.

Important context / recent signals:
- Last month we saw 2x peak token/sec from a paid customer during a marketing surge; autoscaler handled it but cold starts spiked latency beyond 200ms p95 for ~18 minutes.
- Dedicated pool utilization baseline: p50 62%, p95 88% across all datasets (Feb day-average telemetry).
- We have $Xk unused committed GPU hours from Q1 credits (ops-internal).

Quick numbers (back-of-envelope):
- Single A100-80GB equiv throughput ~ 2.4M tokens/hour (seq-length 1024, mix of chat + completion).
- Current committed pool: 18 GPUs -> ~43.2M tokens/hr theoretical.
- Typical burst demand window: 15–30 minutes.

Forecast scenarios (for reservation sizing):
- Scenario A (Conservative): steady growth +10% month-over-month; aim to reserve for p75 steady-state. Reserve target: 14 GPUs.
  - Rationale: reduce wasted hours, rely on burst/spare capacity for short peaks.
- Scenario B (Balanced): growth +25% momo; reserve to cover p90 steady-state + 20% buffer. Reserve target: 20 GPUs.
  - Rationale: avoids frequent autoscaler ramp and reduces p95 latency exposure.
- Scenario C (Aggressive): growth +50% momo or one large customer commit; reserve 26 GPUs (covers observed marketing surge scenario).
  - Rationale: higher cost but predictable latency and lower throttling risk for enterprise customers.

Burst policy sketches (things to table and test):
- Burst window cap: allow up to +40% instantaneous capacity for 10 minutes, then throttle to baseline with token-backoff.
- Graceful fallback: when burst capacity exhausted, route heavy requests to compatible lower-cost model variant (quantized) automatically.
- Cost guardrail: if burst spend > $Y/day, trigger manual review + rollback.
- Autoscaler cooldown: set to 120s for scale-up (fast) and 600s for scale-down (slow) to avoid flapping.

Assumptions to validate (and how):
- Assumption 1: Short bursts are dominated by a small set of customers (10% of tenants).
  - Validate with telemetry: top-10 tenant token/sec tags (run query for last 90 days).
- Assumption 2: KV cache hit-rate improves effective throughput by ~25% for chat workloads.
  - Validate with canary workload that toggles cache on/off for 4x 1h windows.
- Assumption 3: Quantized model fallback retains acceptable quality for <5% of requests.
  - Validate via automated eval on representative prompts (QA + code gen).

Sim jobs to run (owner / estimate):
- S1: replay last marketing surge (6h) on local cluster with current burst cap configs. Owner: Derek. ETA: 2026-02-25.
- S2: synthetic top-10 tenant spike test (15m bursts x 10). Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2026-02-27.
- S3: alternate autoscaler cooldowns comparison (120s vs 60s vs 180s). Owner: me (Aisha). ETA: 2026-03-02.

Questions for Marcus / Sofia in 1:1:
- Marcus: Do we have a hard SLA baseline that forces us to prioritize p95 latency over cost for specific customer tiers?
- Sofia: How flexible are reserved capacity billing windows if we propose a mid-quarter top-up for Scenario C? Any penalties?
- Both: Are there existing enterprise deals that would prefer predictable provisioning (we can propose discounted reserved blocks)?

Proposed next actions (post-meeting):
- Action 1: Approve sim S1 and S2 to run this week. Deliverables: replay logs + tail-latency plot. Owner: Derek + Marcus. Due: 2026-02-28.
- Action 2: Draft reservation proposal doc for finance with Scenario B as default and Scenario C optional (include cost delta + switching plan). Owner: me (Aisha). Due: 2026-03-05.
- Action 3: Create alert for burst-spend > $Y/day and add runbook stub. Owner: SRE (assign via ops ticket RWI-INF-801). Due: 2026-03-03.
- Action 4: Short customer outreach to top-3 tenants flagged in S2 to align expectations. Owner: CS (Sofia). Due: 2026-03-06.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- Consider temporary discount program for customers that agree to shift heavy background jobs to off-peak windows (evening credits).
- Think about pre-warming KV caches for expected traffic windows via lightweight TTL refresh job.
- Metric to push to console: ratio of burst-extension minutes to reserved GPU-minutes (new KPI).

Open risks:
- Over-reserving increases committed costs and may be politically hard with finance.
- Under-reserving + aggressive throttles could cause CS escalations and churn for enterprise accounts.

Slack / links to run before meeting:
- query: ops-telemetry > top-tenant-token-rate (last 90d)
- linear: RED-342 (forecasting viz pipeline)
- jira: RWI-INF-789 (autoscaler tuning backlog)

Follow-up format (what I'll share after meeting):
- 1-page summary: chosen scenario + why, experiments green-lit, action owners & dates.
- Raw sim outputs + config diffs attached to linear ticket.

Random scratch thoughts (dump):
- Maybe we can productize a ‘burst credits’ feature for customers who want short-term predictable bursts — sell as add-on.
- Keep some spare capacity in a low-cost region as a last-resort overflow; need network egress cost check.

---
End of scratch notes.

(Will tidy into a proper proposal after 1:1 — these are messy, expect typos and TODOs.)
